_: SLIT-SCAN CINEMA — one COMPLETE SWEEP becomes ONE FRAME. This cannot run in real time and that is intrinsic rather than a limitation to engineer away: a sweep takes seconds and a frame lasts a twelfth of one. So it is an OFFLINE RENDER — run a short sweep, keep the finished tape as a frame, clear, run the next. The clip keeps playing throughout, so consecutive frames are built from consecutive stretches of footage and the film MOVES: the subject turns, the composition shifts, and every single frame is a whole scan rather than a moment. Keep `duration` short (1-1.5s) — it is the exposure of one frame, and 24 of them at 12fps is two seconds of film for about ninety seconds of rendering. frames MUST be 1: a stack here would be a window inside a frame that is already a whole sweep. The render loop lives outside the surface; this spec is the per-frame exposure.
